context: Tests whether the agent correctly maps common Vercel build failure symptoms to the specific fixes prescribed in the rapid-deploy skill's Common Build Failures table, including where to find build logs.

checklist.name: TypeScript fix instruction
checklist.description: For the 'Type error: Property X does not exist' symptom, instructs fixing the TypeScript error in the flagged file (not e.g. suppressing with @ts-ignore)

checklist.name: Env var → Vercel settings fix
checklist.description: For the 'Environment variable not defined' symptom, instructs adding the variable to Vercel project settings (not just the local .env file)

checklist.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_URL named
checklist.description: Explicitly names `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_URL` as the variable to add to Vercel settings for the second failure

checklist.name: Module not found → npm install
checklist.description: For the 'Module not found' symptom, instructs running `npm install` and committing the updated `package-lock.json`

checklist.name: package-lock.json commit
checklist.description: Specifically mentions that the updated `package-lock.json` must be committed (not just that npm install should be run)

checklist.name: Case-sensitivity for ENOENT
checklist.description: For the file import casing issue (Components/Button vs components/Button), identifies Linux case-sensitivity as the cause and instructs checking file casing

checklist.name: Build logs location
checklist.description: Explains that build logs are found by opening the deployment in the Vercel dashboard and clicking 'Build Logs'

checklist.name: Vercel dashboard path
checklist.description: Refers to the Vercel dashboard → Deployments tab as a place to access deployments and their logs

checklist.name: Does NOT suggest --noEmit workaround
checklist.description: Does NOT suggest disabling TypeScript strict checks, adding @ts-ignore, or using --noEmit as a permanent solution to TypeScript errors

checklist.name: No unrelated troubleshooting
checklist.description: Does NOT include troubleshooting steps for symptoms not present in the task (e.g. network errors, authentication failures) — stays focused on the four given symptoms
